Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups related to data handling and retention that came up in the call:

- Procurement asked for SOC2 evidence and a proposed contract clause for retention limits.

Can you confirm the specifics so we can put together a proposed retention schedule and contract language? From memory you said: 0-retention for PII/PHI request payloads, short retention (days) for metadata/diagnostic logs, and metrics allowed for 30+ days if anonymized. Is that correct? Also: do you require data residency in a specific region (we noted us-east-1 on the call)?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the retention buckets (PII 0-retention vs. metadata 7d vs. metrics 30d).
- I’ll loop in Camila (SE) and Rafael (Legal/Sales) to propose a technical implementation and contract language.

Thanks - happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:04:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention follow-up / post-demo notes

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the summary - that matches what we talked about. A bit more detail from the privacy team so your legal/SE folks have clarity: 

- PII/PHI: zero retention of request payloads that contain PHI/PII. We need assurance that payloads are not stored in any logs, persisted caches, or long-term KV. Short-lived in-memory processing is acceptable if it is not written to disk and is immediately purged after inference.
- Request metadata & diagnostics: we can allow retention for debugging (IP, timestamp, model id, non-content metadata) for up to 7 days. These must be masked/hashed where feasible.
- Metrics & aggregates: anonymized usage/quality metrics (latency percentiles, token counts, aggregate error rates) are fine to keep for 30+ days.
- Data residency: all processing and any temporary logs must remain in us-east-1.
- Compliance artifacts: we’ll need your latest SOC2 Type II report and a draft of the retention language to give to procurement/legal.

Procurement (CC’d) will handle contract clauses and BAA if PHI is in scope.

Cheers,
Laura Chen
Head of Data Privacy | Acme Health
laura.chen@acmehealth.com

Laura -

Appreciate the clarity. Looping in Camila (SE) to outline the implementation options and Rafael to own the contract/BAA side.

High-level proposal (attached as a spreadsheet for your review):
- PII/PHI request payloads: 0-retention. Implementation option A: we do not write request bodies to disk or logs; bodies are processed in-memory and immediately purged. Option B (if you require request de-identification before transit): we can accept pre-redacted inputs or provide an edge-side redaction hook.
- Metadata/diagnostics: retain non-content metadata for 7 days (configurable) - stored in encrypted logs with masked identifiers.
- Aggregated metrics: retain anonymized metrics for 30 days (extendable on request).
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral by default; can be configured to zero retention for routes handling PHI.
- Key management: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest.

Attachments included: proposed-retention-schedule.xlsx (detailed buckets + config options) and our latest SOC2 Type II summary PDF.

Questions for you:
1) When you say "0-retention" do you need zero persistent storage of payloads only, or does the policy require no transient logging either (we can support both; no transient write vs. in-memory only)?
2) Are there any additional fields in request metadata that must be redacted before storage?

Next steps: Rafael will draft suggested contract language and a BAA template; Camila will provide an engineering note describing how we enforce zero retention per-route. We’ll aim to get those over by EOD Tuesday (Jun 15).

Thanks - Marissa\n--
Attachments: proposed-retention-schedule.xlsx; SOC2-type2-2026.pdf
